key_insight: LongAgent turns longitudinal patient data analysis into a guided search problem, using history-aware decision making to better predict future outcomes. The core idea is to identify and reuse the most informative past signals across irregular, heterogeneous medical records.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of predicting future medical outcomes from longitudinal data that is heterogeneous, sparsely sampled, and spread across multiple sources. Traditional approaches often struggle to select predictive variables and integrate time-varying information effectively.
method: Uses a history-guided agentic search strategy to explore longitudinal patient records.
Selects informative variables and temporal patterns from heterogeneous, irregularly sampled medical data.
Integrates evidence across time to build representations that support outcome prediction.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a more adaptive way to model complex healthcare timelines without relying only on fixed feature engineering. It is especially useful for prediction tasks where the most relevant signals are scattered, noisy, and time-dependent.
visual_elements: A timeline of patient records with irregular event spacing and multiple data sources.
An agent/search flow diagram showing history-guided selection of useful variables.
A before-vs-after comparison of raw longitudinal data versus learned predictive representation.
An outcome prediction pipeline icon set: data sources -> agent -> representation -> prediction.
paper_title: LongAgent: History-Guided Agentic Search for Longitudinal Outcome Prediction
paper_authors: Siyao Wang, Florian Guitton, Shuojie Fu, Guanyu Tao, Kai Sun
